justification: Stops the precinct-keying churn permanently: (1) adds a Waverley rule (column_copy: v2_precinct_id := v2_dcp_part for E-parts) to the derivation pass — needed because the daily re-extraction cron had already superseded Waverley's 07-28 keyed generation and nulled the keys; (2) wires the derivation pass to RUN AUTOMATICALLY as step [4/4] of the post-extraction enrichment block, so any re-extraction re-derives precinct keys instead of leaving them NULL. This is the fix for docs/EXTRACTION_WHY_IT_RECURS: re-extraction is now non-destructive to keying without human action.

pre_impl.existing_data: Live forensics: Waverley current gen = 264 rows, 0 keyed, but v2_dcp_part='E1'..'E6' present; superseded gen = 885 rows keyed (the 07-28 work the cron overwrote). Boundaries E1-E5,E7. After --apply: 5/6 reconnect (E1-E5); E7 stays orphan (re-extraction dropped the cadastre-derived Edina Estate content — the pass correctly does not invent it). Enrichment already auto-runs post-extraction (actionability/layer/applicability); keying is the missing 4th step.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If a re-extraction changes v2_dcp_part semantics the copy would mis-key; column_copy only fires when the value matches ^E[0-9], and the extraction sets v2_dcp_part deterministically per Part.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: column_copy is a 3rd derivation strategy alongside the existing ones; the auto-run reuses the enrichment block's existing post-commit hook point.

functions.name: _derive
functions.output: the column value when it matches the regex (Waverley E1..E7), else None
functions.if_none: non-matching/NULL v2_dcp_part yields None -> row untouched

functions.name: main
functions.input: args.council; runs after actionability/layer/applicability on a passed commit
functions.output: calls derive_precinct_keys.run(council, apply=True) so committed rows get keyed
functions.if_none: wrapped in try/except — a keying failure is non-fatal and prints a warn, never blocks extraction

values.value: waverley_part_e rule: column_copy of v2_dcp_part matching ^E[0-9]$|^E[0-9]
values.if_missing: Waverley would remain unkeyed after re-extraction (the pre-fix state)

queries.purpose: select Waverley rows carrying an E-part to key
queries.where_clause: WHERE is_current=true AND source_council='waverley' AND v2_dcp_part ~ '^E[0-9]'

break_it.scenario: The daily re-extraction cron runs and supersedes the newly-keyed Waverley rows again with unkeyed ones.
break_it.what_happens: Without the auto-run wiring, Waverley silently un-keys every night (the bug just observed).
break_it.how: The derivation pass now runs as enrichment step [4/4] on every commit, so the cron re-keys Waverley itself immediately after re-extracting.
break_it.repro: run the extractor in commit mode for waverley and confirm the [4/4] keying step keys the E-parts

break_it.scenario: The auto-run keying raises (e.g. transient DB error) mid-cron.
break_it.what_happens: It could abort the whole extraction run if unguarded.
break_it.how: The [4/4] call is wrapped in try/except and prints a non-fatal warning; extraction and enrichment already completed and committed.
break_it.repro: point DATABASE_URL at an unreachable host during the keying step

break_it.scenario: Auto-run applies a validate:False rule (Ashfield ch-D page-range) after a re-extraction.
break_it.what_happens: The ch-D rows get page-derived keys.
break_it.how: Correct in this context: after a re-extraction the rows are fresh/unkeyed, so the page rule is the right keying (no hand-patch to overwrite). The footgun guard only concerns applying it against existing hand-patched rows.
break_it.repro: re-extract ashfield chapter-d and confirm [4/4] keys by page

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - Waverley 5/6 boundaries now serve (E1-E5); next cron re-extraction of any keyed council keeps its keys via [4/4].
